key_insight: CT–CS energy alignment controls the trade-off between charge generation and voltage loss in organic solar cells, while triplet recycling determines whether that balance persists at device level.
engineering_relevance: The model suggests targeting LE–CT offsets of 0.15–0.20 eV, weakly exothermic CT–CS offsets of 0.05–0.075 eV, and CT–T offsets no greater than about 0.1 eV.
method: Couple singlet/triplet exciton kinetics with device drift–diffusion transport.
Solve state populations and reversible transitions self-consistently.
Evaluate energy offsets and triplet-transfer kinetics in transient and steady-state operation.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports reproduction of triplet-mediated recombination in PM6:Y6 and material-dependent triplet recycling in D18:NFA blends, without quantitative accuracy metrics.
watch_item: The proposed energy-offset windows are model-based design guidance; the abstract does not establish their generality across organic photovoltaic materials or report AI methods.
paper_title: Device Model Linking Singlet and Triplet Spin-State Properties to Organic Photovoltaic Device Characteristics
